title: Conformal calibration: ONE-SIDED lower bound with fail-safe warmup
description: IMPLEMENT per forecasting.md 4.1: one-sided lower bound only (under-prediction is the harmful direction); k>n => quantile 1 => lo=0 (fail-safe, can never be actionable); warmup => lo=point but state=warming; censored resolution for intervals truncated by an incident; discard_pending on recovery; ACI alpha update. Output: eta_point_s (display), eta_lower_bound_s (policy), calibration.state warming|calibrated|degraded. TESTS: A2 bound assertion, warming-never-actionable, fail-safe k>n. REFS: forecasting.md 4.1, schemas/forecast.schema.json, .tmp/storage_ballast_helper/src/monitor/conformal.rs.
notes:
[2026-10-23 10:28:55 UTC] COVERS: MP-REQ-024, MP-REQ-050 (lead time).
---
[2026-10-23 10:31:34 UTC] RISK / FAILURE MODES (conformal):
- R1 Under-prediction is the harmful direction; a two-sided interval silently rewards early warnings and punishes late ones equally. Defence: one-sided lower bound only.
- R2 Small-n quantile invents confidence. Defence: k>n => q=1 => lo=0 => never actionable (fail-safe).
- R3 Warming leak: a point estimate presented as a bound. Defence: schema forces actionable=false when state=warming; test asserts it.
- R4 Censoring: an interval truncated by an incident is not a normal sample. Defence: censored resolution + discard_pending on recovery; ACI alpha update.

DONE MEANS: bound assertion A2 green; k>n fail-safe test green; warming-never-actionable test green.

EXIT: MP-REQ-020..026 pass, replay vs naive baseline on trace corpus. REFS: docs/03-algorithms/telemetry-model.md, pressure-estimator.md, forecasting.md; schemas/forecast.schema.json, pressure-state.schema.json.
notes:
[2026-10-23 10:35:51 UTC] EXECUTION ORDER: P2SAMPLE -> P2STATE -> P2RATE -> P2FORECAST -> P2CONFORMAL -> P2EPROC -> P2CONTRACT. The order is forced: a forecast without a rate has nothing to project; a bound without a forecast has nothing to bound; an actionable gate without a bound cannot be written safely.

CENTRAL RULE: only the lower bound may drive action. The point estimate is a display artifact. Any code path that lets eta_point_s reach the policy layer is a bug even if it produces plausible numbers.

WARMING: a warming calibration produces a displayable point and a NULL bound, and must therefore be non-actionable. This is the single most likely place for a "helpful" regression.

THE V1 FENCE (read v1-scope-contract.md section 2 before writing any code): T1/T2/T4-framework/L2-managed/T5 are in. T3 act, L3 allowlist-terminate, L4 auto-intervention, and suspend-as-relief are OUT and have no executor code path. The single legal signal call site is stopOwnedChild(OwnedPid) per ADR-014 section 2. Adding any other signal path is not a code review decision; it is an ADR.

ORDERING TRAP: do not build T4/L2 before P4EXEC's intent-durability and breaker machinery exists. Both paths are externally effective; without intent records a crash makes them un-auditable, and without separate breaker classes a flaky adapter silently disables admission control.

MODE DISCIPLINE: everything here plans in observe from day one and only executes in canary after evidence. Enforce is never a default.

RISK: without this, verification and refusals become un-auditable, and the "no success without measurement" rule becomes unenforceable in practice.
DONE MEANS: explain golden output identical before/after deleting non-ledger state.

Coverage must be visible next to every attribution claim, because a confident attribution over 40% coverage is a lie with good formatting.

LEAK VS PRESSURE: growth is not a leak. A suspicion carries alternatives and a what-would-change-mind, and authorises nothing.

title: Executor + actionguard: TOCTOU, rate limits, breakers, intent durability
description: IMPLEMENT the execution contract exactly: health, mode, decision age, precondition recheck, rate limit, breaker, then perform with timeout; durable intent fsync BEFORE performing (refuse intent_not_durable); result record with 5 outcomes; budgets charged on execution not approval; per-class breakers. TESTS: T-AA-4..8, ST-5..ST-10, intent-recovery idempotency. REFS: action-authorization.md sections 4/6/7, schemas/action-result.schema.json.
notes:
[2026-10-23 10:28:55 UTC] COVERS: MP-REQ-043, MP-REQ-044, MP-REQ-046.
---
[2026-10-23 10:31:34 UTC] RISK / FAILURE MODES (executor):
- R1 Crash between intent and result: must not silently lose an attempt. Defence: durable intent fsync first, unknown_crash_window on recovery, charges budget, exactly-once.
- R2 TOCTOU: state changes between plan and execute. Defence: re-read every precondition immediately before performing; refuse on any flip.
- R3 Approval-counted budgets: budgets charged on approval let a misconfigured planner exhaust a budget without acting (observed in sbh: 1165 approvals, 15 deletions). Defence: charge on execution only.
- R4 Config loosening mid-incident: a policy edit must not retroactively authorize a recorded decision, nor tighten a live safety invariant. Defence: decision carries a policy snapshot; executor checks snapshot + invariants + live health/mode.
- R5 Crash loop storm: restart resets counters. Defence: persisted counters.

DONE MEANS: T-AA-4..8, ST-5..ST-10, recovery-run-3-times test.
